name: Northumberland

licensing.selective: Selective licensing in the Croft area of Blyth (between Hodgsons Road, Waterloo Road/Bridge Street, Regent Street and Renwick Road) from 14 October 2024 for five years, to October 2029. No selective licensing elsewhere in the county; Ashington Town Council has asked for a scheme there.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme found; national mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people from two or more households) applies.

housing: South-east Northumberland, around Blyth, Ashington and Bedlington, has rows of former colliery terraces with a sizeable private rented sector, and the Croft area of Blyth is now under selective licensing. Cramlington is a new town of estates that is still growing. Further north and west, Morpeth, Hexham, Alnwick and Berwick are stone-built market towns, and the rural uplands and the coast have stone cottages, farm lets and many holiday homes. Many rural homes are off the gas grid.
checkinTips: Colliery terraces in Ashington, Blyth and Bedlington: photograph damp at the base of walls, back yards, outhouses and rear lanes.
Homes in Blyth's Croft licensing area: note the licence number and check that the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms are there and working.
Coastal homes in Blyth, Amble and Berwick: record salt marks and rust on window fittings and damp on exposed walls.
Stone cottages and farm lets in the hills and Tyne Valley: photograph stoves, chimneys, oil tanks or LPG supply with the fuel level, and any septic tank.
Cramlington's estate homes: note garages, parking bays, fences and any shared paths.
Former holiday cottages let long term on the coast: list furniture and kitchenware item by item, as much is often included.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Northumberland County Council's housing standards team.
